claims: Artemis II is NASA's crewed mission to orbit the Moon.
Artemis II has a duration of approximately 10 days.
Artemis II launched from Kennedy Space Center, FL.
The crew of Artemis II consists of Reid Wiseman (NASA), Victor Glover (NASA), Christina Koch (NASA), and Jeremy Hansen (CSA - Canadian Space Agency).
Artemis II validates the Orion spacecraft's life-support systems.
Artemis II tests the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft with a crew.
Artemis II is the first crewed lunar flyby since 1972.
The crew of Artemis II will travel around the far side of the Moon.
Artemis II will break records for the farthest distance humans have traveled from Earth.
Artemis II tests critical systems including the Universal Waste Management System.
The Universal Waste Management System reportedly experienced a minor fault light shortly after launch.
The crew of Artemis II will conduct organ-on-a-chip studies to analyze radiation impacts on health.
The crew of Artemis II will deploy four international satellites.
Artemis I was an uncrewed flight in 2022.
Artemis III lunar landing is planned.
